clue.text: Pooh-pooh journalist's return journey

indicators.note: return means the journalist's abbreviation is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist
a ride is a journey on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: A reporter scoffs at the trip home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ED into DE, which then comes before RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh something is to dismiss it with scorn, which is to mock it.

clue.text: Had a vision about fur wrap for a wonderful girl

indicators.note: about means the word for vision goes round the wrap

parts.note: dreamt means had a vision while asleep
a boa is a long fur or feather stole

explanation.surface: Someone imagined a stole for a lovely woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts BOA inside DREAMT, before its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat is a slang term for a very attractive person.

clue.text: Allied with Rex, and exultant

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king
elated means joyful, exultant

explanation.surface: Joined with the king and thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Related means connected, linked by kinship or association.

clue.text: Godsends — eg extraordinary persistence

indicators.note: extraordinary means the letters of the two words are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Lucky breaks, for instance remarkable perseverance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggedness is stubborn determination, the quality of keeping going.

clue.text: City position still producing great joy

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, its position on a postal map
static means not moving, still

explanation.surface: A fixed place in the financial district makes someone thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: The City (capital C) is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ecstatic is rapturous, the state that intense delight produces.

clue.text: Stop mad Dane in the row of trees

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation stop

indicators.note: mad means the letters of the word for a Scandinavian are jumbled

explanation.surface: Halt the crazy Scandinavian in the avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade is a row of columns, and by extension a line of trees planted at regular intervals.

clue.text: Wine put in to sweeten things

indicators.note: put in to means the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: Adding wine to make things sweeter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent is a deep-red Spanish wine, once used as communion wine.

clue.text: Modify a painting technique

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or modify

explanation.surface: Alter a method of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is painting with pigments bound in egg yolk, a medium and method.

clue.text: May gets on as a rule

parts.note: can means may, be permitted to
taken as written

explanation.surface: The month of May proceeds as normal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a general rule or principle.

clue.text: Tinker bowled a length

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
an ell is an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A mender of pots was bowled for a long distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinker Bell is the fairy in Peter Pan; the definition takes the first half of her name for the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinker Bell, the Peter Pan fairy, links the two words as a well-known name.

clue.text: Clue — eg. "wild about love" in pastoral poem

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes around the letter for love
wild means the letters of the two words run riot into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A crossword hint, for instance 'wild about love', points to a rustic verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' shuffles CLUE and EG into ECLGUE; 'about' puts O inside it, after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short poem of shepherds and country life, the classic pastoral form.

clue.text: Connexion, married — if old, he was a source of light

definitions.text: he was a source of light

parts.note: a link is a connection (connexion is the older spelling)
man as in 'man and wife', a married male, a husband

explanation.surface: A married link, the clue suggests, once lit the way in old times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if old' flags that the sense is historical: a linkman carried a link, a flaming torch, to light people through dark streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Before street lighting, torch-bearers were hired to guide walkers home at night.

clue.text: Artist going round the native country

indicators.note: going round means the painter's name encloses the next word

parts.note: George Morland was an 18th-century English painter of rural scenes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter tours the land of his birth.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist is George Morland, an English painter; his name wraps round THE.
explanation.definitionFit: One's homeland, the country of one's birth, is often called by a parental image.

clue.text: A point about age

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
on means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A remark about how old someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immensely long period, an age in the geological or poetic sense.

clue.text: Where Houdini bought his equipment?

parts.note: the escapologist Houdini needed fetters, so his supplier would be a shop selling them, punning on a retail term for a branch of a group

explanation.surface: Asking where the great escapologist shopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiple retailer with many branches is named the same way as a shop selling fetters.

clue.text: The Devil's familiar jokes

definitions.meaning: Old One is a nickname for Satan, so this reads as the Devil's own name with a possessive
chestnuts, jokes heard many times before

explanation.surface: Satan's tired gags.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 'Devil's' sounds the same as the plural, so 'Old One's' stands for the answer spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devil is nicknamed the Old One, and stale gags are known as old ones, both well-worn idioms.

clue.text: Incidental illustration, when mounted, is a joy

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means the word is lifted, read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
delight is great joy

explanation.surface: A side picture, framed and hung, is a pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mounted' turns IS into SI in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is incidental information that throws extra light on a subject.

clue.text: A bench to get across

parts.note: a thwart is the seat across a rowing boat, a bench for the rower

explanation.surface: A seat lets you cross over.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart is a nautical word for from side to side, crosswise.

clue.text: Between you and me, it might help your solving

definitions.text: Between you and me, it might help your solving

parts.words: Between you and me, it might help your solving
parts.note: reads as a confidential tip, but means a direct mind-to-mind link between setter and solver

explanation.surface: A whispered hint to the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought transfer between minds would let a solver read the setter's intentions.

clue.text: Secured confidence, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for confidence is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: trust is confidence placed in someone

explanation.surface: Someone gained assurance, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means tied up tightly, fastened with rope or binding.

clue.text: A 1 dn rising note to hoot

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: the answer to 1 down is a wonderful girl, and a lulu is a remarkable person or thing
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A gorgeous girl climbing a scale gives a cry.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to 1 Down's definition, a wonderful girl, for LULU. 'rising' turns A LULU into ULULA.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to howl or wail, like an owl's call.

clue.text: Laced it afresh, in adjectival order

indicators.note: afresh means the letters of the two words are laced up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Retying a shoe in a grammatically proper sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: the answer is the adjective from 'edict', an order.
explanation.definitionFit: Edictal describes anything relating to an edict, a decree, so it is the adjective of that kind of command.

clue.text: Loiter loosely round female -in clover, maybe

indicators.note: round means the anagram goes around the letter for female
loosely means the letters of the word for hang about are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Hang about idly around a woman in a field of clover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' makes TREOIL from LOITER; 'round' puts F inside, after TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trefoil is any three-leaved plant, clover being the best-known example.

clue.text: Share a common boundary with a reservation

parts.note: a 'but' is an objection or reservation, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Neighbouring land on a native reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to lie adjacent, touching at an edge.

clue.text: Girl takes exercises to get fit

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
PT, physical training, is exercise

explanation.surface: A young woman works out to get in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt is to adjust or make suitable, to tailor something to a purpose.

clue.text: Sinister woman has a record with scoundrels

parts.note: black means wicked or sinister
she is a pronoun for a woman
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A villainous woman with a criminal record keeps bad company.
explanation.definitionFit: Black sheep are disreputable members of a family or group, the ones who bring shame.

clue.text: Young "un, left in bed

indicators.note: in means the letter for left is put inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A youngster left lying in their bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A colt is a young male horse, and by extension a youthful novice.

clue.text: The bird is flown

parts.note: reads as the phrase for someone having escaped, but describes a bird of prey that shares its name with a toy flown on a string

explanation.surface: The prisoner has escaped.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a bird of prey and also a toy flown in the wind on a string.

clue.text: A catch is about to go astray — how humiliating!

indicators.note: about means the word for catch goes round the word for going astray

parts.note: to bag is to catch, as a hunter bags game
to sin is to stray morally, go astray

explanation.surface: Dropping an easy catch is embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SIN inside BAG, after its A, giving BASING.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasing means lowering in dignity, the effect of something degrading.

clue.text: Boor receives no approval as an observer

indicators.note: receives means the word for boor takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a lout is a boorish, uncouth man
O, a zero, means nothing or no
OK is a word of approval

explanation.surface: An oaf gets no approval for being a spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' puts OOK inside LOUT, after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a person posted to watch, a sentry or watcher.

clue.text: Oddly, Crete, not Italy gave us this art style

definitions.text: Italy gave us this art style

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of the two words are arranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: Strangely, a Greek island rather than Italy produced this artistic school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italy' looks like part of the wordplay with 'not', but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trecento is the 14th century in Italian art, the period of Giotto.

clue.text: I mean what I say about a friend

parts.note: re means concerning, about
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are sincere about a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is used to stress sincerity, like 'honestly' or 'truly'.
